newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan airport controllers go slow to delay flights.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan airport controllers go slow to delay flights.

text.p: Air traffic controllers who launched a go-slow crippling Kenya's main airports on Saturday continued their action on Sunday, stranding tourists and other passengers.
Arriving flights were delayed clearance to land for several hours, and some services were diverted to neighbouring Tanzania, airport officials said.

The controllers said they had launched their go-slow in support of demands for more pay. They said promises of improved pay and working conditions, made after a similar go-slow last December, had not been met.
Meteorologists who supply weather information have also launched a go-slow, increasing the problems of the airline industry.

The strikes increased pressure on a government rocked by an International Monetary Fund (IMF) decision on Thursday to halt a $205 million aid package to Kenya, citing concern over high-level corruption.
Tourism is Kenya's biggest hard currency earner with 717,000 visitors in 1996.
